claims.text: The starting composite consists of connected tungsten particles or regions within a copper matrix for fusion-reactor joint applications.
Tungsten particles will be coated with a thin nickel interlayer by electroless plating before spark-plasma sintering.
The nickel interlayer is reactive during sintering.
Spark-plasma sintering will be conducted at 1200–1400 °C.
Sintering will be conducted under vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
The proposed irradiation and thermal-cycling tests will be representative of fusion-reactor joint service.
Ni-rich intermetallic phases will form at the W/Cu interface during sintering.
Reaction of the deposited nickel layer will create a compositionally graded intermetallic interface.
The graded Ni-rich interface will improve the wettability of copper on tungsten.
Improved copper wettability will reduce interfacial voids and phase separation.
Reduced voiding and improved interfacial contact will enhance thermal transport.
Improved interfacial contact will maintain mechanical integrity under irradiation and thermal cycling.
Relative to W–Cu made without the nickel interlayer, the nickel-treated composite will have lower W/Cu interfacial porosity.
Relative to the baseline, the nickel-treated composite will have higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to the baseline, the nickel-treated composite will have superior mechanical durability under cyclic irradiation and thermal loads.
Vapor-coated tungsten powders sintered with copper without a tailored nickel interlayer constitute an existing fabrication baseline.
Processing will remain below tungsten's melting point.
The resulting composite is intended to withstand high irradiation doses and repeated thermal cycling in fusion-reactor joints.
